metadata.name: locate
metadata.displayName: locate - Find files by name (database search)
metadata.description: Find files quickly using a prebuilt name database

installation.note: On Ubuntu, locate is typically provided by plocate (newer) or mlocate (older). The database is updated by updatedb (often via a daily timer/cron).

overview.summary: The locate command searches a system-wide database of filenames, making it much faster than scanning the filesystem with find. Because it uses a database snapshot, results can be outdated until the database is updated.
when_to_use: Quickly find where a file might be located by name
Search for man pages, configs, or binaries by filename
Find files across the whole system when speed matters

syntax.description: Patterns are matched against the file database. Use options to control case sensitivity, limit results, or require existing paths.

misconceptions.title: locate searches the filesystem live
misconceptions.misconception: locate is always accurate because it scans the disk like find
misconceptions.reality: locate searches a database snapshot, so it can show deleted files or miss newly created ones until the database is updated.
misconceptions.tip: Run updatedb (often with sudo) or wait for the scheduled update if results seem wrong.
